claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 in the as-cast state has a hierarchical heterostructure.
The HfNbTiVAl10 heterostructure contains spatial variations in atomic packing, bond strength, and elastic moduli.
Variance measures of atomic planar density, ionization energy, elastic moduli, and the D parameter can be supplied as features to a random-forest or similar machine-learning model.
Variance in atomic planar density reflects nonuniform atomic packing.
Variance in ionization energy reflects nonuniform bond strength.
Variance in elastic moduli reflects nonuniform stiffness and localized deformation under stress.
The D parameter captures competition between dislocation emission and brittle fracture and is informative for plasticity.
Variance features allow a machine-learning model to correlate local heterogeneity with macroscopic mechanical behavior.
Variance-inclusive models represent dislocation dynamics, yielding, and fracture more robustly than models relying only on mean properties.
The variance-inclusive machine-learning model will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior in HfNbTiVAl10 more accurately than established simulations.
The variance-inclusive machine-learning model will predict those properties more rapidly than established simulations.
The enhanced model will reduce prediction errors by approximately 10–15% relative to conventional simulations.
The enhanced model will reduce computational time by more than 50% relative to conventional simulations.
Established comparison simulations use traditional average-based inputs without explicitly representing hierarchical microstructural variability.
The predictive advantage should occur only when a pronounced hierarchical heterostructure governs the alloy's mechanical behavior.
The predictive advantage may disappear when the microstructure is predominantly homogeneous or processing-induced defects dominate the response.
